note:
HTML Title renders a limited, admin-controlled allowlist of inline HTML tags inside node titles (and via an html_title field formatter / node_html_title Views handler). Its only settings config is html_title.settings:allow_html_tags (space-separated tag string, shipped default '
'), edited at /admin/config/user-interface/html_title (permission 'administer html title settings'). The filtering is done by the html_title.filter service (Drupal\html_title\HtmlTitleFilter::decodeToText/decodeToMarkup), which decodes entities then Xss::filter()s against that allowlist. Medium cases read back live config (a known allowlist value; a field whose view display uses the html_title formatter); hard cases mutate live config (add the tag to the allowlist; switch a field's view-display formatter to html_title).

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site I enabled the html_title module. Which configuration object and key store the list of HTML tags allowed in node titles, what is the shipped default value, and at what admin path do I edit it?
evals.expected_output:
The config is html_title.settings, key allow_html_tags, a space-separated tag string whose shipped default is '
'. Edit it at /admin/config/user-interface/html_title (route html_title.settings, permission 'administer html title settings').

evals.prompt: How does the html_title module render markup inside a node title safely, and which service would I call to filter a title string myself? Name the service id and a method.
evals.expected_output: It decodes the stored title (Html::decodeEntities) then runs Xss::filter() limited to the configured allowlist, stripping everything else. Call the html_title.filter service (Drupal\html_title\HtmlTitleFilter): decodeToText() for a filtered string or decodeToMarkup() for safe Markup.

evals.prompt: Besides node titles, how can html_title render a plain-text (string) field's value as HTML in a view display, and how does it affect the node Title column in a Views listing?
evals.expected_output: It ships an 'html_title' field formatter (label 'HTML-title text') for string fields — select it on the field's Manage display. It also swaps the Views node-title field handler to node_html_title via hook_views_data_alter, so any view showing the node Title field renders the decoded markup automatically.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which HTML tags are currently allowed inside node titles by the html_title module? Inspect the live configuration and list them.
evals.expected_output: html_title.settings:allow_html_tags is '<em> <strong> <cite>', so em, strong and cite are the currently-allowed tags.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has a plain string field field_hty_known. Inspect the live default view display for Article and state which field formatter renders that field.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_hty_known component uses the html_title formatter ('HTML-title text').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, editors need to italicise words inside node titles using <em>, but the html_title allowlist currently does not permit it. Update the html_title configuration so that the <em> tag is allowed in node titles, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output:
Add to html_title.settings:allow_html_tags (e.g. set it to '
' via the settings form or `drush config:set html_title.settings allow_html_tags ' '`). The verify checks the live allowlist now contains .

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a plain string field field_hty_task that currently renders as plain text. Using the html_title module, configure the Article default view display so this field's value is rendered as HTML markup, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default set the field_hty_task component's formatter type to html_title (the 'HTML-title text' formatter) and save. The verify checks the component type is html_title.
